function.text: ABCB11 encodes bile salt export pump. function.text: ABL1 encodes tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1. somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving ABL1 have been reported in acute myeloid leukemia, chronic myeloid leukemia, and b-lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma.

function.text: ACADS encodes acyl-CoA dehydrogenase short chain. Based in part on similarity, short-chain specific acyl-CoA dehydrogenase is one of the acyl-CoA dehydrogenases that catalyze the first step of mitochondrial fatty acid beta-oxidation, an aerobic process breaking down fatty acids into acetyl-CoA and allowing the production of energy from fats. The first step of fatty acid beta-oxidation consists in the removal of one hydrogen from C-2 and C-3 of the straight-chain fatty acyl-CoA thioester, resulting in the formation of trans-2-enoyl-CoA.

germline.text: Germline disease associations include short chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase deficiency (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving ACADS have been reported in glioblastoma, low-grade glioma, and colorectal carcinoma.

function.text: ACVR1B encodes activin receptor type-1B. It transduces the activin signal from the cell surface to the cytoplasm and is thus regulating a many physiological and pathological processes including neuronal differentiation and neuronal survival, hair follicle development and cycling, FSH production by the pituitary gland, wound healing, extracellular matrix production, immunosuppression and carcinogenesis. Activin binds to type-2 receptor at the plasma membrane and activates its serine-threonine kinase.

somatic.text: Sequence mutations in ACVR1B have been reported in pituitary tumors.

function.text: ATG2B encodes autophagy-related protein 2 homolog B. Based in part on similarity, it is a lipid transfer protein required for both autophagosome formation and regulation of lipid droplet morphology and dispersion. It tethers the edge of the isolation membrane (IM) to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) and mediates direct lipid transfer from ER to IM for IM expansion. function.text: ATP6AP1 encodes v-type proton ATPase subunit S1. Based in part on similarity, V-ATPase is responsible for acidifying and maintaining the pH of intracellular compartments and in some cell types, is targeted to the plasma membrane, where it promotes acidification of the extracellular environment. It guides the V-type ATPase into specialized subcellular compartments, such as neuroendocrine regulated secretory vesicles or the ruffled border of the osteoclast, thereby regulating its activity.

function.text: BCL6 encodes a transcriptional repressor important for germinal-center B-cell development and regulation of differentiation and DNA-damage-response programs. It forms complexes with different corepressors and histone deacetylases to repress the transcriptional expression of different subsets of target genes. It represses its target genes by binding directly to the DNA sequence 5'-TTCCTAGAA-3' (BCL6-binding site) or indirectly by repressing the transcriptional activity of transcription factors. An important function is to allow GC B-cells to proliferate very rapidly in response to T-cell dependent antigens and tolerate the physiological DNA breaks required for immunoglobulin class switch recombination and somatic hypermutation without inducing a p53/TP53-dependent apoptotic response.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving BCL6 have been reported in diffuse large b-cell lymphoma, nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma, and DLBCL / high-grade b-cell lymphoma with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements.

function.text: CBL encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase CBL. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of many signaling pathways by mediating ubiquitination of cell surface receptors. somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving CBL have been reported in chronic myelomonocytic leukemia, juvenile myelomonocytic leukemia, and acute myeloid leukemia.

function.text: CCT8 encodes chaperonin containing TCP1 subunit 8. function.text: CDK8 encodes cyclin-dependent kinase 8. function.text: CDKN2A produces structurally distinct tumor-suppressor proteins through alternative first exons and reading frames. The p16INK4A product inhibits cyclin-dependent kinase activity, whereas p14ARF stabilizes p53 by interacting with MDM2, a ubiquitin ligase that promotes p53 degradation. Both products contribute to G1 cell-cycle control through different mechanisms. This transcript structure is biologically important because a change in the locus can affect the two protein products differently.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving CDKN2A have been reported in thymoma, chordoma, and angiosarcoma.

function.text: CENPA encodes histone H3-like centromeric protein A. It is a histone H3-like nucleosomal protein that is specifically found in centromeric nucleosomes. It replaces conventional H3 in the nucleosome core of centromeric chromatin that serves as an assembly site for the inner kinetochore. The presence of CENPA subtly modifies the nucleosome structure and the way DNA is wrapped around the nucleosome and gives rise to protruding DNA ends that are less well-ordered and rigid compared to nucleosomes containing histone H3.

function.text: DCTN1 encodes dynactin subunit 1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the dynactin complex that activates the molecular motor dynein for ultra-processive transport along microtubules. It contributes to dynein-mediated retrograde transport of vesicles and organelles along microtubules by recruiting and tethering dynein to microtubules. It binds to both dynein and microtubules providing a link between specific cargos, microtubules and dynein.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Perry syndrome (autosomal dominant); amyotrophic lateral sclerosis type 1 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving DCTN1 have been reported in ALK-positive histiocytosis.

function.text: DCUN1D1 encodes DCN1-like protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of an E3 ubiquitin ligase complex for neddylation. function.text: DDB1 encodes DNA damage-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it participates in DNA repair and protein ubiquitination, as part of the UV-DDB complex and DCX (DDB1-CUL4-X-box) complexes, respectively. It is a core component of the UV-DDB complex (UV-damaged DNA-binding protein complex), a complex that recognizes UV-induced DNA damage and recruits proteins of the nucleotide excision repair pathway (the NER pathway) to initiate DNA repair. The UV-DDB complex preferentially binds to cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers (CPD), 6-4 photoproducts (6-4 PP), apurinic sites and short mismatches.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with White-Kernohan syndrome (autosomal dominant).

function.text: DES encodes desmin. Based in part on similarity, it contributes to maintaining the structure of sarcomeres, inter-connecting the Z-disks and forming the myofibrils, linking them not only to the sarcolemmal cytoskeleton, but also to the nucleus and mitochondria, thus providing strength for the muscle fiber during activity. It is required for nuclear membrane integrity, via anchoring at the cell tip and nuclear envelope, resulting in maintenance of microtubule-derived intracellular mechanical forces. It contributes to the transcriptional regulation of the NKX2-5 gene in cardiac progenitor cells during a short period of cardiomyogenesis and in cardiac side population stem cells in the adult.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with dilated cardiomyopathy 1I (autosomal dominant); myofibrillar myopathy 1 (autosomal dominant).

function.text: DGCR8 encodes the non-catalytic RNA-binding component of the microprocessor complex, which carries out an early step in microRNA production. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the microprocessor complex that acts as a RNA- and heme-binding protein that is involved in the initial step of microRNA (miRNA) biogenesis. It forms part of the microprocessor complex that is required to process primary miRNA transcripts (pri-miRNAs) to release precursor miRNA (pre-miRNA) in the nucleus. The heme-bound DGCR8 dimer binds pri-miRNAs as a cooperative trimer (of dimers) and is active in triggering pri-miRNA cleavage, whereas the heme-free DGCR8 monomer binds pri-miRNAs as a dimer and is much less active.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving DGCR8 have been reported in Wilms tumor, pineoblastoma, and wilms' tumor.

function.text: DMRT1 encodes doublesex- and mab-3-related transcription factor 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that plays a key role in male sex determination and differentiation by controlling testis development and male germ cell proliferation. It plays a central role in spermatogonia by inhibiting meiosis in undifferentiated spermatogonia and promoting mitosis, leading to spermatogonial development and allowing abundant and continuous production of sperm. It acts both as a transcription repressor and activator: prevents meiosis by restricting retinoic acid (RA)-dependent transcription and repressing STRA8 expression and promotes spermatogonial development by activating spermatogonial differentiation genes, such as SOHLH1.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with 46 XY differences of sex development (autosomal dominant); spermatogenic failure (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving DMRT1 have been reported in spermatocytic tumor.

function.text: DNMT3B encodes DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase 3B. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase that mediates genome-wide de novo methylation and which is essential for the establishment of DNA methylation patterns during development. It modifies DNA at CpG sites with selectivity for residues flanking the target CpG site at positions -1 and +1, and strong preference for a guanine (G) immediately following the CpG sites. It methylates DNA in a non-cooperative processive manner, allowing the enzyme to diffuse along DNA and methylate multiple sites before dissociation.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with immunodeficiency-centromeric instability-facial anomalies syndrome 1 (autosomal recessive).

function.text: DOCK8 encodes dedicator of cytokinesis protein 8. function.text: DROSHA encodes the catalytic ribonuclease III component of the microprocessor complex. In the nucleus, it cleaves primary microRNA transcripts to release stem-loop precursor microRNAs. DROSHA therefore acts early in the microRNA-production pathway, working with an RNA-binding partner rather than carrying out all of the steps needed to produce mature microRNAs.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving DROSHA have been reported in Wilms tumor, pineoblastoma, and wilms' tumor.

function.text: EPC1 encodes enhancer of polycomb homolog 1. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the NuA4 histone acetyltransferase (HAT) complex, a multiprotein complex involved in transcriptional activation of select genes principally by acetylation of nucleosomal histones H4 and H2A. function.text: ERBB2 encodes HER2, a receptor tyrosine kinase in the epidermal growth factor receptor family. Rather than binding a growth-factor ligand independently, HER2 forms heterodimers with ligand-bound family members and strengthens downstream signaling. function.text: EZH2 encodes the catalytic methyltransferase component of polycomb repressive complex 2, which methylates histone H3 lysine 27 to regulate transcriptional repression. Based in part on similarity, it is a catalytic subunit of the PRC2/EED-EZH2 complex, a Polycomb group (PcG) complex that methylates 'Lys-9' (H3K9me) and 'Lys-27' (H3K27me) of histone H3, leading to transcriptional repression of the affected target gene. It displays a preference for substrates with less methylation, loses activity when progressively more methyl groups are incorporated into H3K27, H3K27me0 > H3K27me1 > H3K27me2. Compared to EZH1-containing complexes, it is more abundant in embryonic stem cells and plays a major role in forming H3K27me3, which is required for embryonic stem cell identity and proper differentiation.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Weaver syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving EZH2 have been reported in follicular lymphoma, primary myelofibrosis, and acute myeloid leukemia.

function.text: FAN1 encodes Fanconi-associated nuclease 1. function.text: FAS encodes tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 6. The adapter molecule FADD recruits caspase CASP8 to the activated receptor. The resulting death-inducing signaling complex (DISC) performs CASP8 proteolytic activation which initiates the subsequent cascade of caspases (aspartate-specific cysteine proteases) mediating apoptosis. FAS-mediated apoptosis may have a role in the induction of peripheral tolerance, in the antigen-stimulated suicide of mature T-cells, or both.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving FAS have been reported in malignant lymphoma, cervical squamous cell carcinoma, and diffuse large b-Cell lymphoma, NOS.

function.text: FBXO11 encodes f-box only protein 11. It is a substrate recognition component of a SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins, such as DTL/CDT2, BCL6, SNAI1 and PRDM1/BLIMP1. The SCF(FBXO11) complex mediates ubiquitination and degradation of BCL6, thereby playing a role in the germinal center B-cells terminal differentiation toward memory B-cells and plasma cells. The SCF(FBXO11) complex also mediates ubiquitination and degradation of DTL, an important step for the regulation of TGF-beta signaling, cell migration and the timing of the cell-cycle progression and exit.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with intellectual developmental disorder with dysmorphic facies and behavioral abnormalities (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving FBXO11 have been reported in Burkitt lymphoma, malignant lymphoma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

function.text: FBXW7 encodes f-box/WD repeat-containing protein 7. It is a substrate recognition component of a SCF (SKP1-CUL1-F-box protein) E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins. function.text: HLA-C encodes HLA class I histocompatibility antigen, C alpha chain. Based in part on similarity, it typically presents intracellular peptide antigens of 9 amino acids that arise from cytosolic proteolysis via proteasome. It can bind different peptides containing allele-specific binding motifs, which are mainly defined by anchor residues at position 2 and 9. The low affinity peptides compete with the high affinity peptides impeding KIR-mediated inhibition and favoring lysis of infected cells.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving HLA-C have been reported in diffuse large b-Cell lymphoma, NOS.

function.text: KAT8 encodes lysine acetyltransferase 8. function.text: KIF26B encodes kinesin family member 26B. Based in part on similarity, it is essential for embryonic kidney development. It contributes to the compact adhesion between mesenchymal cells adjacent to the ureteric buds, possibly by interacting with MYH10. This could lead to the establishment of the basolateral integrity of the mesenchyme and the polarized expression of ITGA8, which maintains the GDNF expression required for further ureteric bud attraction.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving KIF26B have been reported in glioblastoma, low-grade glioma, and ovarian carcinoma.

function.text: KIT encodes a receptor tyrosine kinase activated by stem cell factor. Its structure includes extracellular immunoglobulin-like domains, a membrane-spanning region, and an intracellular kinase domain. Activation triggers phosphorylation of downstream proteins controlling proliferation, differentiation, migration, and apoptosis. KIT has normal roles in blood-cell formation, stem-cell maintenance, germ-cell development, pigmentation, and mast-cell biology, explaining its involvement in several distinct tissue contexts.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with gastrointestinal stromal tumor (autosomal dominant); piebaldism (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving KIT have been reported in mucosal melanoma, thymic carcinoma, and mast cell sarcoma.

function.text: KLHL6 encodes kelch-like protein 6. It is a substrate-specific adapter of a BCR (BTB-CUL3-RBX1) E3 ubiquitin ligase complex that acts as a multifunctional regulator of B-cell receptor (BCR) signaling, germinal center formation, and T-cell function. It targets the BCR signaling subunits CD79A and CD79B for ubiquitin-mediated degradation, thereby controlling surface BCR homeostasis.

somatic.text: KLHL6 mutations have been reported in chronic lymphocytic leukemia.

function.text: KMT2A encodes a histone methyltransferase that helps establish H3K4 methylation and regulate transcriptional programs important for development and hematopoiesis. Based in part on similarity, it is a histone methyltransferase that plays an essential role in early development and hematopoiesis. It is a catalytic subunit of the MLL1/MLL complex, a multiprotein complex that mediates both methylation of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4me) complex and acetylation of 'Lys-16' of histone H4 (H4K16ac). It catalyzes methyl group transfer from S-adenosyl-L-methionine to the epsilon-amino group of 'Lys-4' of histone H3 (H3K4) via a non-processive mechanism.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Wiedemann-Steiner syndrome (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving KMT2A have been reported in thymoma, myeloid sarcoma, and acute myeloid leukemia.

function.text: LIG4 encodes DNA ligase 4. It catalyzes the NHEJ ligation step of the broken DNA during DSB repair by resealing the DNA breaks after the gap filling is completed. It joins single-strand breaks in a double-stranded polydeoxynucleotide in an ATP-dependent reaction. LIG4 is mechanistically flexible: it can ligate nicks as well as compatible DNA overhangs alone, while in the presence of XRCC4, it can ligate ends with 2-nucleotides (nt) microhomology and 1-nt gaps.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with DNA ligase IV deficiency (autosomal recessive).

function.text: LYN encodes tyrosine-protein kinase Lyn. It is required for the initiation of the B-cell response, but also for its down-regulation and termination.

function.text: MITF encodes microphthalmia-associated transcription factor. It is a transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of melanocyte survival and differentiation as well as melanosome biogenesis. It binds to M-boxes (5'-TCATGTG-3') and symmetrical DNA sequences (E-boxes) (5'-CACGTG-3') found in the promoter of pigmentation genes, such as tyrosinase (TYR). It participates in the cellular response to amino acid availability by acting downstream of MTOR: in the presence of nutrients, MITF phosphorylation by MTOR promotes its inactivation.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Waardenburg syndrome type 2 (autosomal dominant); Waardenburg syndrome type 2A (autosomal dominant).

function.text: MKI67 encodes proliferation marker protein Ki-67. Based in part on similarity, it is a protein that associates with the surface of mitotic chromosomes and acts both as a chromosome repellent during early mitosis and chromosome attractant during late mitosis. The MKI67 brush structure prevents chromosomes from collapsing into a single chromatin mass by forming a steric and electrostatic charge barrier: the protein has a high net electrical charge and acts as a surfactant, dispersing chromosomes and enabling independent chromosome motility. It binds DNA, with a preference for supercoiled DNA and AT-rich DNA.

function.text: MLLT1 encodes protein ENL. function.text: MRE11 encodes double-strand break repair protein MRE11. Based in part on similarity, it is a core component of the MRN complex, which plays a central role in double-strand break (DSB) repair, DNA recombination, maintenance of telomere integrity and meiosis. The MRN complex is involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR), an error-free mechanism which primarily occurs during S and G2 phases. The complex (1) mediates the end resection of damaged DNA, which generates proper single-stranded DNA, a key initial steps in HR, and is (2) required for the recruitment of other repair factors and efficient activation of ATM and ATR upon DNA damage.

germline.text: Germline disease associations include ataxia-telangiectasia-like disorder 1 (autosomal recessive).

function.text: MSH6 encodes a MutS-family mismatch-repair protein that forms a mismatch-recognition complex with MSH2. The complex binds and releases mismatched DNA through a nucleotide-dependent molecular switch involving exchange of ADP and ATP. MSH6 contains a conserved nucleotide-binding motif that supports this activity. Its role is therefore in recognition and regulated handling of a DNA mismatch, upstream of the steps that remove and replace the incorrect sequence.

germline.text: Germline disease associations include Lynch syndrome (autosomal dominant); Constitutional mismatch repair deficiency (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: Loss of mismatch-repair function involving MSH6 is relevant in colorectal and endometrial carcinomas.

function.text: MYT1L encodes myelin transcription factor 1 like. function.text: NBN encodes nibrin. It forms part of the MRN complex, which plays a central role in double-strand break (DSB) repair, DNA recombination, maintenance of telomere integrity and meiosis. The MRN complex is involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR), an error-free mechanism which primarily occurs during S and G2 phases. The complex (1) mediates the end resection of damaged DNA, which generates proper single-stranded DNA, a key initial steps in HR, and is (2) required for the recruitment of other repair factors and efficient activation of ATM and ATR upon DNA damage.

function.text: NFE2L2 encodes nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that plays a key role in the response to oxidative stress: binds to antioxidant response (ARE) elements present in the promoter region of many cytoprotective genes, such as phase 2 detoxifying enzymes, and promotes their expression, thereby neutralizing reactive electrophiles. The NFE2L2/NRF2 pathway is also activated in response to selective autophagy: autophagy promotes interaction between KEAP1 and SQSTM1/p62 and subsequent inactivation of the BCR(KEAP1) complex, leading to NFE2L2/NRF2 nuclear accumulation and expression of cytoprotective genes. The NFE2L2/NRF2 pathway is also activated during the unfolded protein response (UPR), contributing to redox homeostasis and cell survival following endoplasmic reticulum stress.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with immunodeficiency, developmental delay, and hypohomocysteinemia (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving NFE2L2 have been reported in hepatoblastoma, lung squamous cell carcinoma, and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.

function.text: NTRK2 encodes the TRKB neurotrophin receptor tyrosine kinase, which regulates neuronal survival, differentiation, and function. Based in part on similarity, it is a receptor tyrosine kinase involved in the development and the maturation of the central and the peripheral nervous systems through regulation of neuron survival, proliferation, migration, differentiation, and synapse formation and plasticity. It is a receptor for BDNF/brain-derived neurotrophic factor and NTF4/neurotrophin-4. Alternatively can also bind NTF3/neurotrophin-3 which is less efficient in activating the receptor but regulates neuron survival through NTRK2.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, 58 (autosomal dominant); obesity, hyperphagia, and developmental delay (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving NTRK2 have been reported in lung adenocarcinoma, infant-type hemispheric glioma, and NTRK-rearranged spindle cell neoplasm, malignant.

function.text: NUF2 encodes kinetochore protein Nuf2. It functions as a component of the essential kinetochore-associated NDC80 complex, which is required for chromosome segregation and spindle checkpoint activity. It is required for kinetochore integrity and the organization of stable microtubule binding sites in the outer plate of the kinetochore. The NDC80 complex synergistically enhances the affinity of the SKA1 complex for microtubules and may allow the NDC80 complex to track depolymerizing microtubules.

function.text: NXF1 encodes nuclear RNA export factor 1. It participates in the nuclear export of mRNA species bearing retroviral constitutive transport elements (CTE) and in the export of mRNA from the nucleus to the cytoplasm (TAP/NFX1 pathway). The NXF1-NXT1 heterodimer is involved in the export of HSP70 mRNA in conjunction with ALYREF/THOC4 and THOC5 components of the TREX complex. ALYREF/THOC4-bound mRNA is thought to be transferred to the NXF1-NXT1 heterodimer for export.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving NXF1 have been reported in chronic lymphocytic leukemia/Small lymphocytic lymphoma.

function.text: PARP1 encodes poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1. Based in part on similarity, it mediates glutamate, aspartate, serine, threonine, histidine or tyrosine ADP-ribosylation of proteins: the ADP-D-ribosyl group of NAD(+) is transferred to the acceptor carboxyl group of target residues and further ADP-ribosyl groups are transferred to the 2'-position of the terminal adenosine moiety, building up a polymer with an average chain length of 20-30 units. Serine ADP-ribosylation of proteins constitutes the primary form of ADP-ribosylation of proteins in response to DNA damage. It also catalyzes tyrosine ADP-ribosylation of target proteins following interaction with HPF1.

function.text: PIK3CA encodes the p110-alpha catalytic subunit of phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase. The enzyme combines a catalytic subunit with an approximately 85-kDa regulatory subunit and uses ATP to phosphorylate phosphoinositide lipids. Its normal role is therefore to generate lipid signaling products through regulated enzymatic activity. The distinction between catalytic and regulatory components is central to understanding its place in the PI3K signaling pathway.

function.text: PIK3CB encodes phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate 3-kinase catalytic subunit beta isoform. It uses ATP and PtdIns(4,5)P2 (phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate) to generate phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PIP3). function.text: PKHD1 encodes fibrocystin. Based in part on similarity, it promotes ciliogenesis in renal epithelial cells and therefore participates in the tubules formation and/ or ensures the maintenance of the architecture of the lumen of the kidney. It has an impact on cellular symmetry by ensuring correct bipolar cell division through the regulation of centrosome duplication and mitotic spindle assembly and by maintaining oriented cell division (OCD) during tubular elongation through planar cell polarity (PCP) pathway. It promotes cell-cell contact through the positive regulation of PTK2 kinase activity leading to either positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation through the HRAS/RAF1 pathways, or negative regulation of apoptosis through the PDK1/AKT1 pathway.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease (autosomal recessive); polycystic kidney disease 4 (autosomal recessive).

function.text: PRKD1 encodes serine/threonine-protein kinase D1. Based in part on similarity, it phosphorylates the epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) on dual threonine residues, which leads to the suppression of epidermal growth factor (EGF)-induced MAPK8/JNK1 activation and subsequent JUN phosphorylation. It phosphorylates RIN1, inducing RIN1 binding to 14-3-3 proteins YWHAB, YWHAE and YWHAZ and increased competition with RAF1 for binding to GTP-bound form of Ras proteins (NRAS, HRAS and KRAS). It acts downstream of the heterotrimeric G protein beta/gamma-subunit complex to maintain the structural integrity of the Golgi membranes, and is required for protein transport along the secretory pathway.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with congenital heart defects and ectodermal dysplasia (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving PRKD1 have been reported in polymorphous adenocarcinoma, cribriform adenocarcinoma of salivary gland, and colorectal adenocarcinoma.

function.text: PTEN encodes a tumor suppressor that removes a phosphate from phosphatidylinositol-3,4,5-trisphosphate, reducing the cellular abundance of this signaling lipid. This activity opposes AKT signaling. Although PTEN contains a domain related to protein tyrosine phosphatases, it preferentially acts on phosphoinositide substrates. Its lipid-phosphatase activity therefore provides a direct biochemical mechanism for restraining a pathway that promotes cellular growth and survival.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with PTEN hamartoma tumor syndrome (autosomal dominant); Cowden syndrome 1 (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving PTEN have been reported in endometrioid carcinoma of endometrium, prostate adenocarcinoma, and prostate.

function.text: RAB35 encodes ras-related protein Rab-35. Based in part on similarity, the small GTPases Rab are key regulators of intracellular membrane trafficking, from the formation of transport vesicles to their fusion with membranes. Rabs cycle between an inactive GDP-bound form and an active GTP-bound form that is able to recruit to membranes different sets of downstream effectors directly responsible for vesicle formation, movement, tethering and fusion. RAB35 is involved in the process of endocytosis and is an essential rate-limiting regulator of the fast recycling pathway back to the plasma membrane.

function.text: RAD50 encodes DNA repair protein RAD50. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the MRN complex, which plays a central role in double-strand break (DSB) repair, DNA recombination, maintenance of telomere integrity and meiosis. The MRN complex is involved in the repair of DNA double-strand breaks (DSBs) via homologous recombination (HR), an error-free mechanism which primarily occurs during S and G2 phases. The complex (1) mediates the end resection of damaged DNA, which generates proper single-stranded DNA, a key initial steps in HR, and is (2) required for the recruitment of other repair factors and efficient activation of ATM and ATR upon DNA damage.

function.text: RAD51C encodes a member of the RAD51 family involved in homologous recombination and DNA repair. function.text: RBBP8 encodes DNA endonuclease RBBP8. Based in part on similarity, HR is restricted to S and G2 phases of the cell cycle and preferentially repairs DSBs resulting from replication fork collapse. It is a key determinant of DSB repair pathway choice, as it commits cells to HR by preventing classical non-homologous end-joining (NHEJ). It specifically promotes the endonuclease activity of the MRN complex to clear DNA ends containing protein adducts: recruited to DSBs by NBN following phosphorylation by CDK1, and promotes the endonuclease activity of MRE11 to clear protein-DNA adducts and generate clean double-strand break ends.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with Jawad syndrome (autosomal recessive).

function.text: RBM15 encodes RNA-binding protein 15. Based in part on similarity, it is an RNA-binding protein that acts as a key regulator of N6-methyladenosine (m6A) methylation of RNAs, thereby regulating different processes, such as hematopoietic cell homeostasis, alternative splicing of mRNAs and X chromosome inactivation mediated by Xist RNA. It contributes to m6A methylation, possibly by binding target RNAs and recruiting the WMM complex. It participates in random X inactivation mediated by Xist RNA: acts by binding Xist RNA and recruiting the WMM complex, which mediates m6A methylation, leading to target YTHDC1 reader on Xist RNA and promoting transcription repression activity of Xist.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving RBM15 have been reported in acute myeloid leukemia.

function.text: REL encodes proto-oncogene c-Rel. NF-kappa-B is a pleiotropic transcription factor which is present in almost all cell types and is involved in many biological processed such as inflammation, immunity, differentiation, cell growth, tumorigenesis and apoptosis. NF-kappa-B is a homo- or heterodimeric complex formed by the Rel-like domain-containing proteins RELA/p65, RELB, NFKB1/p105, NFKB1/p50, REL and NFKB2/p52. The dimers bind at kappa-B sites in the DNA of their target genes and the individual dimers have distinct preferences for different kappa-B sites that they can bind with distinguishable affinity and specificity.

function.text: RICTOR encodes rapamycin-insensitive companion of mTOR. function.text: RNF8 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase RNF8. It is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that plays a key role in DNA damage signaling via 2 distinct roles: by mediating the 'Lys-63'-linked ubiquitination of histones H2A and H2AX and promoting the recruitment of DNA repair proteins at double-strand breaks (DSBs) sites, and by catalyzing 'Lys-48'-linked ubiquitination to remove target proteins from DNA damage sites. function.text: RRAGC encodes ras-related GTP-binding protein C. It is a guanine nucleotide-binding protein that plays a crucial role in the cellular response to amino acid availability through regulation of the mTORC1 signaling cascade. It forms heterodimeric Rag complexes with RagA/RRAGA or RagB/RRAGB and cycles between an inactive GTP-bound and an active GDP-bound form: RagC/RRAGC is in its active form when GDP-bound RagC/RRAGC forms a complex with GTP-bound RagA/RRAGA (or RagB/RRAGB) and in an inactive form when GTP-bound RagC/RRAGC heterodimerizes with GDP-bound RagA/RRAGA (or RagB/RRAGB). This is a crucial step in the activation of the MTOR signaling cascade by amino acids.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving RRAGC have been reported in non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

function.text: RTEL1 encodes regulator of telomere elongation helicase 1. It functions as an anti-recombinase to counteract toxic recombination and limit crossover during meiosis. It regulates meiotic recombination and crossover homeostasis by physically dissociating strand invasion events and thereby promotes noncrossover repair by meiotic synthesis dependent strand annealing (SDSA) as well as disassembly of D loop recombination intermediates. It also disassembles T loops and prevents telomere fragility by counteracting telomeric G4-DNA structures, which together ensure the dynamics and stability of the telomere.

function.text: SETD5 encodes histone-lysine N-methyltransferase SETD5. function.text: SF3B1 encodes a component of the U2 small nuclear ribonucleoprotein complex that participates in branch-point recognition during pre-mRNA splicing. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the 17S U2 SnRNP complex of the spliceosome, a large ribonucleoprotein complex that removes introns from transcribed pre-mRNAs. The 17S U2 SnRNP complex (1) directly participates in early spliceosome assembly and (2) mediates recognition of the intron branch site during pre-mRNA splicing by promoting the selection of the pre-mRNA branch-site adenosine, the nucleophile for the first step of splicing. Sequence independent binding of SF3A and SF3B subcomplexes upstream of the branch site is essential, it may anchor U2 snRNP to the pre-mRNA.

somatic.text: Somatic SF3B1 mutations occur in myelodysplastic neoplasms, particularly those with ring sideroblasts.

function.text: SLC25A13 encodes electrogenic aspartate/glutamate antiporter SLC25A13, mitochondrial. It is a mitochondrial electrogenic aspartate/glutamate antiporter that favors efflux of aspartate and entry of glutamate and proton within the mitochondria as part of the malate-aspartate shuttle. function.text: SMARCA1 encodes SWI/SNF-related matrix-associated actin-dependent regulator of chromatin subfamily A member 1. function.text: SMARCB1 encodes a nuclear tumor-suppressor protein within a chromatin-remodeling complex. function.text: SOCS2 encodes suppressor of cytokine signaling 2. It is a substrate-recognition component of a cullin-5-RING E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complex (ECS complex, also named CRL5 complex), which mediates the ubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of target proteins, such as EPOR and GHR. It specifically recognizes and binds phosphorylated proteins via its SH2 domain, promoting their ubiquitination. The ECS(SOCS2) complex acts as a key regulator of growth hormone receptor (GHR) levels by mediating ubiquitination and degradation of GHR, following GHR phosphorylation by JAK2.

function.text: SPOP encodes a substrate-recognition adaptor for a CUL3-based ubiquitin-ligase assembly. Its MATH domain recognizes short consensus sequences in protein substrates, while its BTB region and an adjacent helical structure support CUL3 binding. SPOP can form dimers, allowing multiple substrate-recognition sites to cooperate. This architecture connects selective substrate binding with ubiquitination, while distinguishing the adaptor from the catalytic functions of the complete ligase assembly.

germline.text: Pathogenic germline variants are associated with neurodevelopmental disorder with relative macrocephaly and with or without cardiac or endocrine anomalies (autosomal dominant); neurodevelopmental disorder with microcephaly and dysmorphic facies (autosomal dominant).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving SPOP have been reported in prostate adenocarcinoma, prostate, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma.

function.text: SPRTN encodes DNA-dependent metalloprotease SPRTN. Based in part on similarity, it is a DNA-dependent metalloendopeptidase that mediates the proteolytic cleavage of covalent DNA-protein cross-links (DPCs) during DNA synthesis and mitosis, thereby playing a key role in maintaining genomic integrity. DPCs are highly toxic DNA lesions that interfere with essential chromatin transactions, such as replication and transcription, and which are induced by reactive agents, such as UV light or formaldehyde. It associates with the DNA replication machinery and specifically removes DPCs during DNA synthesis.

function.text: SRC encodes proto-oncogene tyrosine-protein kinase Src. Based in part on similarity, it is a non-receptor protein tyrosine kinase which is activated following engagement of many different classes of cellular receptors including immune response receptors, integrins and other adhesion receptors, receptor protein tyrosine kinases, G protein-coupled receptors as well as cytokine receptors. It participates in signaling pathways that control a diverse spectrum of biological activities including gene transcription, immune response, cell adhesion, cell cycle progression, apoptosis, migration, and transformation. Receptor clustering or dimerization leads to recruitment of SRC to the receptor complexes where it phosphorylates the tyrosine residues within the receptor cytoplasmic domains.

function.text: SRF encodes serum response factor. function.text: SRP72 encodes signal recognition particle subunit SRP72. Based in part on similarity, it forms part of the signal recognition particle (SRP) complex, a ribonucleoprotein complex that mediates the cotranslational targeting of secretory and membrane proteins to the endoplasmic reticulum (ER). The SRP complex interacts with the signal sequence in nascent secretory and membrane proteins and directs them to the membrane of the ER. The SRP complex targets the ribosome-nascent chain complex to the SRP receptor (SR), which is anchored in the ER, where SR compaction and GTPase rearrangement drive cotranslational protein translocation into the ER.

function.text: TDG encodes G/T mismatch-specific thymine DNA glycosylase. It is a DNA glycosylase that plays a key role in active DNA demethylation: specifically recognizes and binds 5-formylcytosine (5fC) and 5-carboxylcytosine (5caC) in the context of CpG sites and mediates their excision through base-excision repair (BER) to install an unmethylated cytosine. It is also involved in DNA repair by acting as a thymine-DNA glycosylase that mediates correction of G/T mispairs to G/C pairs: in the DNA of higher eukaryotes, hydrolytic deamination of 5-methylcytosine to thymine leads to the formation of G/T mismatches. It is capable of hydrolyzing the carbon-nitrogen bond between the sugar-phosphate backbone of the DNA and a mispaired thymine.

function.text: TERC produces the RNA template component of telomerase. The telomerase ribonucleoprotein combines this template with a reverse-transcriptase protein component to add TTAGGG repeats at chromosome ends. TERC therefore supplies sequence information for telomere extension rather than the catalytic protein itself. Regulation of telomerase activity is linked to telomere maintenance and cellular senescence.

germline.text: Pathogenic constitutional TERC variants cause autosomal dominant dyskeratosis congenita, a telomere biology disorder associated with bone-marrow failure.

somatic.text: Somatic copy-number gain involving the TERC region has been associated with progression of cervical neoplasia to invasive carcinoma. Regional gain is distinct from the constitutional loss-of-function mechanisms underlying telomere biology disorders.

function.text: TERT encodes the catalytic reverse-transcriptase component of telomerase. Telomerase is a ribonucleoprotein enzyme essential for the replication of chromosome termini in most eukaryotes. It is the catalytic component of the teleromerase holoenzyme complex whose main activity is the elongation of telomeres by acting as a reverse transcriptase that adds simple sequence repeats to chromosome ends by copying a template sequence within the RNA component of the enzyme. It catalyzes the RNA-dependent extension of 3'-chromosomal termini with the 6-nucleotide telomeric repeat unit, 5'-TTAGGG-3'.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving TERT have been reported in liposarcoma, paraganglioma, and chondrosarcoma.

function.text: TFEB encodes transcription factor EB. Based in part on similarity, it is a transcription factor that acts as a master regulator of lysosomal biogenesis, autophagy, lysosomal exocytosis, lipid catabolism, energy metabolism and immune response. It participates in the cellular response to amino acid availability by acting downstream of MTOR: in the presence of nutrients, TFEB phosphorylation by MTOR promotes its cytosolic retention and subsequent inactivation. It specifically recognizes and binds the CLEAR-box sequence (5'-GTCACGTGAC-3') present in the regulatory region of many lysosomal genes, leading to activate their expression, thereby playing a central role in expression of lysosomal genes.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving TFEB have been reported in TFEB-altered renal cell carcinoma.

function.text: TGFBR1 encodes TGF-beta receptor type-1. The SMAD2-SMAD4 complex is subsequently translocated to the nucleus where it modulates the transcription of the TGF-beta-regulated genes.

function.text: TMEM147 encodes transmembrane protein 147. It forms part of the multi-pass translocon (MPT) complex that mediates insertion of multi-pass membrane proteins into the lipid bilayer of membranes. The MPT complex takes over after the SEC61 complex: following membrane insertion of the first few transmembrane segments of proteins by the SEC61 complex, the MPT complex occludes the lateral gate of the SEC61 complex to promote insertion of subsequent transmembrane regions. It also acts as a negative regulator of CHRM3 function, most likely by interfering with its trafficking to the cell membrane.

germline.text: Germline disease associations include neurodevelopmental disorder with facial dysmorphism, absent language, and pseudo-pelger-huet anomaly (autosomal recessive).

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving TMEM147 have been reported in glioblastoma, endometrial carcinoma, and prostate adenocarcinoma.

function.text: TMEM68 encodes DGAT1/2-independent enzyme synthesizing storage lipids. Based in part on similarity, it is a catalytic subunit of the alternative triglyceride biosynthesis pathway, which mediates formation of triacylglycerol from diacylglycerol and membrane phospholipids. It synthesizes triacylglycerol at the expense of membrane phospholipids, such as phosphatidylcholine (PC) and its ether-linked form (ePC), thereby altering the composition of membranes. The alternative triglyceride biosynthesis pathway is probably required to provide the energy required for rapid growth when fuel sources are limiting.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving TMEM68 have been reported in CNS embryonal tumor with PLAG family gene alteration.

function.text: TNFAIP3 encodes tumor necrosis factor alpha-induced protein 3. It is an ubiquitin-editing enzyme that contains both ubiquitin ligase and deubiquitinase activities. It participates in immune and inflammatory responses signaled by cytokines, such as TNF and IL-1 beta, or pathogens via Toll-like receptors (TLRs) through terminating NF-kappa-B activity. function.text: TOP1 encodes DNA topoisomerase 1. Based in part on similarity, it releases the supercoiling and torsional tension of DNA introduced during the DNA replication and transcription by transiently cleaving and rejoining one strand of the DNA duplex. It introduces a single-strand break via transesterification at a target site in duplex DNA. The scissile phosphodiester is attacked by the catalytic tyrosine of the enzyme, resulting in the formation of a DNA-(3'-phosphotyrosyl)-enzyme intermediate and the expulsion of a 5'-OH DNA strand.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving TOP1 have been reported in basal cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma.

function.text: TOPBP1 encodes DNA topoisomerase 2-binding protein 1. Based in part on similarity, it is a scaffold protein that acts as a key protein-protein adapter in DNA replication and DNA repair. function.text: TP53 encodes p53, a tumor-suppressor transcription factor with DNA-binding, transcriptional-activation, and oligomerization domains. In response to cellular stress, p53 changes expression of target genes that control cell-cycle arrest, DNA repair, senescence, apoptosis, and metabolism. Alternative promoters, RNA splicing, and translation initiation produce multiple protein isoforms. These properties allow the gene to connect detection of cellular stress with several distinct growth-control and cell-fate responses.

somatic.text: Somatic TP53 mutations occur across many cancer types.

function.text: TRIM27 encodes zinc finger protein RFP. somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving TRIM27 have been reported in intraductal carcinoma of salivary gland.

function.text: U2AF1 encodes a component of the U2 auxiliary splicing factor that contributes to recognition of 3′ splice sites during pre-mRNA processing. It contributes to both constitutive and enhancer-dependent splicing by mediating protein-protein interactions and protein-RNA interactions required for accurate 3'-splice site selection. It directly mediates interactions between U2AF2 and proteins bound to the enhancers and thus may function as a bridge between U2AF2 and the enhancer complex to recruit it to the adjacent intron.

somatic.text: Recurrent somatic U2AF1 mutations occur in myelodysplastic neoplasms.

function.text: UPF1 encodes regulator of nonsense transcripts 1. Based in part on similarity, it is an RNA-dependent helicase required for nonsense-mediated decay (NMD) of aberrant mRNAs containing premature stop codons and which modulates the expression level of normal mRNAs. It is an ATP-dependent 5'-3' helicase active on RNA:DNA substrates with a 5'-RNA extension. Phosphorylated UPF1 is recognized by EST1B/SMG5, SMG6 and SMG7 which are thought to provide a link to the mRNA degradation machinery involving exonucleolytic and endonucleolytic pathways, and to serve as adapters to protein phosphatase 2A (PP2A), thereby triggering UPF1 dephosphorylation and allowing the recycling of NMD factors.

It is a DNA-binding protein critical for the DNA damage response, specifically in repairing double-strand breaks (DSBs) via the classical non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) pathway. It forms a heterodimer with XRCC6 (Ku70), creating the Ku70:Ku80 heterodimer (Ku complex), which serves as a DNA end-binding complex. It primarily binds DSBs and recruits essential repair factors, assembling the core long-range NHEJ complex to facilitate the alignment and ligation of broken DNA ends.

function.text: YAP1 encodes transcriptional coactivator YAP1. function.text: ZNRF3 encodes E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase ZNRF3. Based in part on similarity, it is an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that acts as a negative regulator of the Wnt signaling pathway by mediating the ubiquitination and subsequent degradation of Wnt receptor complex components Frizzled and LRP6. It acts on both canonical and non-canonical Wnt signaling pathway.

somatic.text: Somatic alterations involving ZNRF3 have been reported in adrenocortical carcinoma.
